Inline Comment
Selection-based comments for DSH Web conversations.
Select text, write a note, and it travels with your next message — as a chip in the composer and in
e a note, and it travels with your next message — as a chip in the composer and in the sent message.
English · 简体中文
DSH Web client plugin · no runtime dependencies · zh / en
## Preview

1 · Select. Drag over any text in a conversation; the Annotate pill appears next to the selection wh
g over any text in a conversation; the Annotate pill appears next to the selection when you release.
2 · Annotate. The quote is pinned in the card. Enter adds the note, Shift+Enter inserts a newline, E
e. The quote is pinned in the card. Enter adds the note, Shift+Enter inserts a newline, Esc cancels.
3 · Attach. The note lands at the end of the composer as one atomic chip, with the caret after it. H
over or click to re-read the quote and note.
4 · Send. Sent messages keep the chip instead of spilling the quote block into the bubble. The model
still receives the readable quote block.
5 · Configure. Settings → General → Comment shortcut switches between Enter and ⌘/Ctrl+Enter.
## Features

- **Select-to-comment** anywhere in a conversation — messages, replies, tool output.
- **One atomic
chip** in the composer, appended at the end with the caret following it; backspace removes the whole

note.
- **Preview on hover or click**, in the composer and after sending: quote and note side by si

de.
- **Chips survive sending.** A user-text rule turns the stored quote block back into the same ca

psule; the model still reads the block.
- **Enter to add, Shift+Enter for a newline** — switchable t

o ⌘/Ctrl+Enter.
- **Theme-aware, localized, zero-config.** Uses host theme tokens and the client loc

ale service (zh / en).
- **No Host surface.** No service, tool, prompt, or session format change.

Requires a DSH profile with the Web client. From the DSH plugin manager:

## Usage
1. Drag over text in a conversation. Release — the **Annotate** pill appears next to the selection.
2. Click it, write the note, and press **Enter** (or **⌘/Ctrl+Enter**). The note is appended to the

composer as a reference chip.
3. Keep typing, or send. The model receives:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

4. Hover the chip at any time to see the quote and the note. Backspace deletes the whole chip from
t

the chip at any time to see the quote and the note. Backspace deletes the whole chip from
the draft.
## Configuration
| Setting | Default | Where |
| Submit shortcut | `Enter` adds, `Shift+Enter` newlines | Settings → General → **Comment shortcut**

|
| Alternative | `⌘/Ctrl+Enter` adds, `Enter` newlines | Same row |
| Quote limit | 320 characters

| `MAX_QUOTE` in `client.js` |
| Note limit | 4000 characters | `MAX_COMMENT` in `client.js` |

The shortcut preference is stored in the browser at
`localStorage["dsh.inline-comment.submit-mode"]`
(`enter` or `mod`) and applies immediately.
## How it works
| Surface | Extension point |

| Floating pill, compose card, preview card | `shell.overlay` |
| Composer bridge (`inputActions`, `

useInput`) | `conversation.input.overlay` |
| Real reference chip | session-scope `slash/input-inser

t-reference` + an `inputTriggers` source |
| Sent-message chip | a `uiConversation.userText` rule +

`conversation.user.text.node` |
| Shortcut row | `settings.general.item` |

A note is appended to the end of the draft by computing the detect offset of the draft end
(referenc

e chips count as one character, command chips by `claim.token`), then inserted through the
same refe

rence-chip path the `@file` picker uses. The chip's `ref` carries the quote and note as
base64url JS

ON, so the draft can be restored, previewed, and serialized after a reload. On send,
the plugin's se

rializer expands the chip into the quote block; on render, the user-text rule
recognizes that block
and renders the capsule again.
## Compatibility

- Built against the DSH desktop client bundled with `0.2.1-rc.5`.
- Client-only: no Host plugin beha

vior, no session format, no tools.
- The chip uses the composer's reference-chip shell (`appearance:

file`) with the file glyph hidden
by a scoped CSS rule. If the host changes that DOM, the chip fall

s back to the file glyph; the
feature keeps working.

preview images.

## Known limitations

- Sent-message recognition is text-level: any hand-written `> quote` + `> 批注：…` block renders as a
c

hip. This is intentional and mirrors how `@file` mentions are recognized.
- Uninstalling the plugin

while a draft still holds an annotation chip makes that draft unsendable
(the serializer is gone). D

elete the chip first.
- The quote is truncated to 320 characters and the note to 4000 before they en

ter the chip.
- The previews are design mocks; visual output follows the host theme.
